t: If any provision of this title or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is held invalid, the remainder of the title and the application of the provision to other persons not similarly situated or to other circumstances shall not be affected thereby.

fable.w: This is a severability clause: it preserves the rest of the title if any provision is held invalid. The tempting reading is that "held invalid" implies litigation, but the clause does not grant any outside party a right to sue or object to a federal decision. It provides for no consultation, hearing, comment, rulemaking, or advisory body involving anyone outside the federal government.

opus.w: This is a boilerplate severability clause. It only says that the rest of the title still stands if one provision is struck down. The words "held invalid" might suggest litigation, but the clause gives no outside party a right to sue or object. It also sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body.
opus.b: This is a standard severability clause. Someone might read "held invalid" as hinting at a lawsuit against the government. That reading doesn't hold up: the clause only says what happens to the rest of the title if a court strikes part of it down. It does not give any outside party a right to sue or a way to take part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This is a standard severability clause. It addresses the legal consequence if a court finds part of the statute invalid, ensuring the rest of the law remains in effect. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: If any provision of this title or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is held invalid, the remainder of the title and the application of the provision to other persons not similarly situated or to other circumstances shall not be affected thereby.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "any person" implies the public is involved, but this is a standard severability clause that deals with the legal validity of the statute itself, not with a process for public input or consultation on a government decision. It does not create any mechanism for outsiders to participate in decision-making.
